MIA'S CURSE
​
03/24/2026 - Update to version 1.1:
A few minor updates:
A few misspelled words have been corrected.
The Purification spell was not curing a couple of late game poison effects, which is now fixed.
Some rooms in the Cauldron Tower had flashing effects that caused some folks to get a game crash. Found in the area with the cut-out doors which you access getting the scissors. This was due to a background flash effect going which I believe was due to lack of a wait. Typically, reloading from a save works, but still can get irksome. Rather than go through each event and test what's going on, my brother decided to remove the background flash effect entirely in those areas.
SECTION A: SYNOPSIS
Spoiler
GAME INFO:
Length: Approximately 20 hours
Genre: JRPG / Dark Fantasy Horror / Explorative Progression / Puzzle Solving
GAME DEVELOPERS:
Happy Halloween! Or belated by the time this gets posted and approved.
The game was planned, designed, programmed, mapped, and written by my brother - Michael (Stimplepimp). My involvement (Andrew, amerk, WindedImp) was co-planning, story assistance, editing, game testing, creating the walkthrough, game deployment and uploading.
The game takes heavy inspiration from several sources - mainly Dragon Quest 1 for the single warrior experience, Zelda for its puzzles, Castlevania and Shadowgate for its horror themes, and Metroid for its progression.
GAME STORY:
Through the darkness you've journeyed long to the gates of a mysterious castle. A strange sense of familiarity grips you as you go forth, knowing in your heart there is one in dire need of your help. Held there by a dark and maleficent force, the Princess of the Dawning Light Mia can only hopelessly watch as an untold nightmare slowly unfolds.
You take the role of the lone hero who must venture through the ruins of a treacherous castle, in search of his lost love - Mia, the Princess of the Dawning Light. As the player, you'll engage in touch encounters / turn-based battles, as you navigate the different layers of the castle, in search of abilities and items that will allow you to progress further. Along the way, you'll get to solve various puzzles, avoid traps, read the lore behind the castle's mysterious past, purchase items and weapons, and help the lone hero put together his own forgotten past.
GAME FEATURES:
Single Character Story -
you play as the lone hero in search of your long lost love trapped inside the ruins of a mysterious castle. Uncover your own memories and past along the way.
Dark atmospheric horror -
with themes inspired by cult favorites in both games and movies.
Turn-based / Touch Encounters -
Enemy sprites are on the field / no invisible encounters.
Paths intertwine and connect throughout the large castle
, - You'll need to find abilities and skills to create shortcuts and open up new areas of the castle.
Solve puzzles, collect treasures and loot, and avoid the traps.
Collect heart pieces and special pieces along the way to maximize your health and skill points. -
Strategize by using these in battle. They will not only boost your HP / SP but restore as you will. So hold onto these for tougher fights and boss battles.
Multiple side content, multiple endings.
A complete walkthrough is included.

posts.author: DrBuni
posts.body: The maps you shared give me Super Mario RPG vibes, which is a great thing in my book. Good stuff!

posts.author: amerk
posts.body:
That was mostly probably due to the look of the sprites and some of the resources my brother was using plus how he mapped a lot of the areas, but now that you mention it, it does sort of have that Mario'ish look. No spoilers, but consider some of the side lore and dark humor in the game, it fits!
Side note, one of the later areas was giving him some trouble when he replayed - flashing effects that would occassionally cause his playthrough to crash. These are in the paper door areas. He said reloading a save and replaying it should work.
But his computer is slowing tanking out, and neither of us had any issues previously except maybe a brief stutter. So it could be his computer, or how it was deployed. He didn't want to throw an update out that removed the effects if it was something related to his computer, so please let us know if there are any problems. If the solution is to keep saving before going through one of the doors, then it's probably better to remove the flash effect in that area.
This would be late in the game - walkthrough that's included refers to the area as the Valley of the Cutouts if you need reference.
